question.summary: The proposed facet completeness is false. The claimed necessity and simultaneous optimality of Fourier-plus-diagonal measurements remain open.
question.importance: The remaining claim would identify the measurement architecture that extracts the strongest and most noise-resistant CGLMP evidence from a maximally entangled state.
question.unresolved: For a fixed maximally entangled state, prove or refute necessity of Fourier-plus-diagonal measurements and their simultaneous white-noise and Kullback-Leibler optimality in every outcome dimension.

claims.title: Part A is refuted by a finite facet counterexample
claims.text: Bancal, Gisin and Pironio find two-party, two-setting, four-outcome facets that are neither CGLMP inequalities nor lower-outcome liftings.

claims.title: Numerics clarify the optimizer but do not prove Part B
claims.text: Global optimization shows that nonmaximally entangled states can outperform maximally entangled ones. The archived measurement claim must therefore retain its fixed-state qualifier.

decisions.rationale: Status assessed against the archived statement in the 2026-08-12 primary-source audit; the evidence ledger lists the results considered.

editorial.interpretation: Part B fixes the maximally entangled state. A better global strategy using a nonmaximally entangled state does not by itself answer that fixed-state measurement question.
